1  State Vs. Jatin Chauhan & Ors.

P  BRIEF STATEMENT OF FACTS FOR THE DECISION:-
 1.

The allegations against accused is that on 27.10.2022 at about 09:20 am at Phool Mandi, Main Gate,
Footpath, Gazipur Village, Delhi within the jurisdiction of PS PIA, accused persons in furtherance of common intention used criminal force to commit theft of gold chain of the complainant and thereby committed offences punishable u/s 356/379/34 IPC.
2.
Investigation was conducted and was concluded by filing the charge sheet.
Copy of challan and relevant documents were supplied to the accused free of costs as envisaged under Section 207 of Cr.P.C.
Arguments on charge were heard and charge u/s 356/379/34 IPC was framed against the accused persons vide order dated 05.07.2024 to which they pleaded not guilty and opted to face trial.

3. In order to bring home the guilt against the accused, prosecution has examined the following witnesses:
 Prosecution Name of the witness Descript  witness No.
 1 Smt. Hemlata Jayant Complainant 4.

During the trial, prosecution had relied upon the following documentary evidence:
Proved by / Exhibit No. Description of the exhibit Attested by 1/A Statement of complainant PW1 1/B Site plan PW1 5.

In the evidence recorded before the court the complainant completely resiled from her previous statement and did not identify the accused persons even when attention of the witness was specifically drawn towards the accused by Ld. APP.
PW1 denied the involvement of the accused.
Thus, PW1 turned hostile and no other independent eyewitness has been cited by the prosecution.
Since the P BHARGAV RAO complainant has turned hostile, no purpose would be served by examining the other witnesses, who are all either police officials and not any public witness.

In this regard, it is pertinent to note the judgment of honourable High Court of Delhi in Govind and Others.
v. State, 104(2003) DLT 510, where it was held that:
"In cases where ultimate chance of conviction is very bleak or there is no prospect of the case ending in conviction in such cases no useful purpose is likely to be served by allowing a criminal prosecution and trial to continue.

sentences.text: It is advisable to truncate or snip the proceedings and save valuable time of the courts.

2 6.
In view of the above, P.E stands closed.
Since nothing incriminating has come on record against the accused, the statement of the accused under Section 313 Cr.P.C. is dispensed with.
7. Final arguments heard.
8. The complainant, who has been examined in court today, has turned hostile, and has not identified the accused persons.
She has indicated that the accused persons have not committed the offence against her.
It is pertinent to note that under Indian law, the evidence of hostile witnesses is not discarded completely.
The legal maxim, "false in uno false in omnibus " is not applicable in India.
With respect to the evidentiary value of hostile witnesses, it was observed by the Apex Court in the case of Rohtash Kumar v. State of Haryana, (2013) 14 SCC 434, as under - "25.

entities.text: Rohtash Kumar v. State of Haryana, (2013) 14 SCC 434
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is a settled legal proposition that evidence of a prosecution witness cannot be rejected in toto, merely because the prosecution chose to treat him as hostile and cross examined him.
The evidence of such witnesses cannot be treated as effaced, or washed off the record altogether.

The same can be accepted to the extent that their version is found to be dependable, upon a careful scrutiny thereof."
9.
Therefore, it has to be seen if the evidence of such hostile witnesses can be relied in part.
In the present case, the evidence available on record is not sufficient to help the prosecution.

PW1 has failed to identify the accused and in absence of her testimony, there is nothing to prove the identity of the accused persons, except their P BHARGAV own disclosure, which is inadmissible in evidence.
Therefore, there is nothing on RAO record to connect the accused with the commission of the offence.
No other independent eyewitness of the incident has been cited and there is no other 17:43:01 +0530 circumstance to point towards the guilt of the accused.
Even if all the other prosecution witnesses were to be examined, the case of the prosecution could not have been proved.
10. In a criminal trial, the onus remains on the prosecution to prove the guilt of accused beyond all reasonable doubts and the benefit of doubt, if any, must necessarily go in favour of the accused.
It is for the prosecution to travel the entire distance from 'may have' to 'must have'.

In the case titled as Dr. S. L. Goswami vs State of Madhya Pradesh, 1972 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 258, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that:
"i) The onus of proving all the ingredients of an offence is always upon the prosecution and at no stage does is shift to the accused.

entities.text: Dr. S. L. Goswami vs State of Madhya Pradesh, 1972 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 258
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is no part of the prosecution duty to somehow hook the crook.
Even in cases where the defence of the accused does not appear to be credible or is palpably false that burden does not become any the less.
ii) The standard of proof to prove a defence plea is not the same as that which rests upon the prosecution.
Where the onus shifts to the accused, and the evidence on his behalf probabilizes the plea he will be entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt".

11. It is a settled law as well as matter of common knowledge that evidence of complainant/ victim and other public witnesses is the best available evidence and the case can be proved beyond State vs Jatin Chauhan on 29 January, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116510658/
3 reasonable doubt on the basis of testimony of said witness only.

In the present case, perusal of entire evidence reveals that complainant has not supported the case of the prosecution and the complainant categorically denied that accused committed any offending act.

12. Keeping in view the overall conspectus of the case, I am of the considered view that the prosecution has miserably failed to discharge the burden imposed on it by law of satisfying this court beyond reasonable doubt of the guilt of the accused persons.

Therefore, I give benefit of doubt to the accused and accordingly, accused Jatin Chauhan S/o Sh. Jilani Chauhan and Samrath S/o Sh.
Mahender Pal
are acquitted of the charge framed u/s 376/356/34 IPC.
